items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "polyploidy"?
options: The possession of more than two complete sets of chromosomes, which can lead to instant sympatric speciation in plants.
A group of organisms with similar morphology, physiology and behaviour that can interbreed to produce fertile offspring and are reproductively isolated from other species.
The use of the number of differences in DNA or protein sequences, and the rate at which they accumulate, to estimate when two species diverged.
The formation of a new species from an existing one.
items.answer: The possession of more than two complete sets of chromosomes, which can lead to instant sympatric speciation in plants.
items.markingKey: Polyploidy: the possession of more than two complete sets of chromosomes, which can lead to instant sympatric speciation in plants.

items.stem: Which gene is commonly used as a marker in modern genetic engineering?
options: A gene for green fluorescent protein (GFP)
items.answer: A gene for green fluorescent protein (GFP)
items.markingKey: GFP fluoresces under UV; replaces antibiotic resistance markers.

items.stem: Diego writes in a revision note: "A 3 : 1 ratio means that exactly three out of every four offspring will show the dominant phenotype." Identify the error and write a correct statement.
items.answer: A ratio gives probabilities; in a small sample the numbers may differ by chance.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: A ratio gives probabilities; in a small sample the numbers may differ by chance. [2]

items.stem: Complete aerobic respiration of one mole of a fatty acid (palmitic acid) releases 9790 kJ. It produces 108 mol of ATP, each storing 31 kJ mol⁻¹. What is the efficiency of ATP production?
A student in Dubai states: "Viruses belong to the domain Bacteria because they are microscopic." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: Viruses are non-cellular and are not classified into any domain.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Viruses are non-cellular and are not classified into any domain. [2]

items.stem: In a typical 28-day menstrual cycle, which event occurs at about day 14?
options: Corpus luteum degenerating; endometrium about to break down
Menstruation; new follicles begin to develop
items.answer: Ovulation
items.markingKey: Day 14: ovulation; LH at its peak.

items.stem: Explain why a hormone affects only certain cells in the body.
items.answer: Only target cells have the specific receptor (on the membrane or inside the cell) that is complementary in shape to the hormone.
items.markingKey: target cells have receptors [1]; complementary shape [1] [2]

items.stem: Elena placed a piece of Elodea in 0.5% sodium hydrogencarbonate solution at 25 °C and counted the bubbles released per minute with a lamp at different distances. Results table. Distance from the lamp / cm: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Number of bubbles per minute, trial 1: 64, 60, 44, 30, 13, 16; trial 2: 64, 61, 45, 30, 22, 16; trial 3: 65, 60, 43, 30, 22, 16. (a) Suggest one way to improve this investigation. (b) Calculate the light intensity at the nearest distance relative to the furthest distance.
items.answer: (a) Collect the gas in a photosynthometer and measure the volume. (b) 36 times greater
items.markingKey: (a) Any one from: collect the gas in a photosynthometer and measure the volume; place a heat filter (beaker of water) between lamp and plant; allow 5 minutes acclimatisation at each distance; repeat each test more times and calculate a mean (to improve reliability); test more values of the distance from the lamp (smaller intervals), especially near the turning point / extremes [1] (b) intensity ∝ 1/d² [1]; (30 ÷ 5)² = 36 [1] [2]

items.stem: Nadia measured the height or mass of individuals in a clone of strawberry plants in Cape Town and found that the data formed a normal distribution. (a) Explain why the data form a normal distribution. (b) Describe how you would decide whether the mean value differs significantly from that of a second population.
items.answer: (a) The characteristic shows continuous variation: it is controlled by many genes (polygenes) with additive effects, plus environmental effects; most individuals are near the mean with few at the extremes. (b) Measure a large random sample from each; calculate means and standard deviations; carry out a t-test with df = n₁ + n₂ − 2; compare t with the critical value at p = 0.05.
items.markingKey: (a) polygenic [1]; additive / environment [1]; most near mean [1] [3] (b) random samples [1]; t-test [1]; compare with critical value [1] [3]

items.stem: cDNA from cancer cells was labelled with a red fluorescent dye and cDNA from normal cells of the same tissue with a green dye. Both were mixed and applied to a microarray. The spots for four genes were: gene R black, gene S green, gene Q yellow, gene T black. (a) Explain why cDNA was made from mRNA rather than using genomic DNA. (b) Suggest how this information could be used in treating cancer. (c) Explain how the cDNA binds to particular spots on the microarray.
items.answer: (a) mRNA is present only for genes being expressed (transcribed); genomic DNA contains all genes whether expressed or not. (b) Genes over-expressed in cancer cells could be targets for drugs; patterns help classify tumour type and choose treatment. (c) Each spot contains many copies of a single-stranded probe; cDNA hybridises by complementary base pairing to its matching probe.
items.markingKey: (a) mRNA shows expression [1]; DNA has all genes [1] [2] (b) Genes over-expressed in cancer cells could be targets for drugs [1]; patterns help classify tumour type and choose treatment [1] [2] (c) Each spot contains many copies of a single-stranded probe [1]; cDNA hybridises by complementary base pairing to its matching probe [1] [2]

items.stem: Kwame is studying meiosis in a maize plant, which has a diploid number of 20. (a) Calculate the number of possible combinations of chromosomes in the gametes due to independent assortment alone. (b) A diploid cell of this organism in G1 contains 7 arbitrary units of DNA. State the DNA content of a cell at the end of meiosis I and of each gamete.
items.answer: (a) 1,024 (b) end of meiosis I: 7 units per cell; gamete: 3.5 units
items.markingKey: (a) 2ⁿ [1] = 2^10 = 1,024 [1] [2] (b) doubled to 14 after S phase, halved at meiosis I = 7 [1]; gamete 3.5 [1] [2]

items.stem: Leila isolated mitochondria from rat liver and suspended them in a buffered solution containing pyruvate, ADP, Pi and oxygen. Over 20 minutes, 8 μmol of pyruvate were completely oxidised. (a) Calculate how many μmol of carbon dioxide were released. (b) Calculate how many μmol of reduced NAD were formed. (c) Name the location within the mitochondrion where the link reaction and Krebs cycle take place.
items.answer: (a) 24 μmol (b) 32 μmol (c) The matrix.
items.markingKey: (a) each pyruvate: 1 CO₂ in link reaction + 2 in Krebs cycle = 3 [1]; 8 × 3 = 24 μmol [1] [2] (b) per pyruvate: 1 (link) + 3 (Krebs) = 4 [1]; 8 × 4 = 32 μmol [1] [2] (c) The matrix [1]

items.stem: Surveys show that the population of the Asian elephant fell from 69,000 in 1970 to 27,300 in 2015. (a) Calculate the percentage decrease in the population. (b) Suggest two likely causes of this decline.
items.answer: (a) 60.4% (b) Habitat loss (deforestation, agriculture); poaching / illegal trade; climate change; pollution; by-catch.
items.markingKey: (a) (69,000 − 27,300) ÷ 69,000 × 100 [1] = 60.4% [1] [2] (b) any 2 from: Habitat loss (deforestation, agriculture); poaching / illegal trade; climate change; pollution; by-catch (1 mark each) [2]

items.stem: Why is potassium hydroxide solution placed in a respirometer?
options: To provide water for the organisms
items.answer: To absorb carbon dioxide
items.markingKey: Movement of the fluid then shows oxygen uptake only.

items.stem: Which type of vector is most often used in gene therapy?
options: A bacterial plasmid in a bacterium
items.answer: A modified (inactivated) virus
items.markingKey: e.g. adeno-associated virus or lentivirus.

items.stem: A student in Lima states: "Fungi are plants because they have cell walls and do not move." Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: Fungi have chitin walls, no chloroplasts and are heterotrophic, so they form a separate kingdom.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Fungi have chitin walls, no chloroplasts and are heterotrophic, so they form a separate kingdom. [2]

items.stem: Tomás extracted chloroplasts from spinach leaves into ice-cold buffer. Equal volumes of chloroplast suspension and DCPIP solution were placed at different distances from a lamp and the time taken for the blue colour to disappear was recorded. Results table. Distance from the lamp / cm: 10, 15, 20, 30, 40. Time for DCPIP to decolourise / s, trial 1: 57, 74, 94, 167, 251; trial 2: 60, 76, 96, 166, 251; trial 3: 58, 72, 98, 169, 260. Suggest one way to improve this investigation.
items.answer: Use a colorimeter to judge the end point.
items.markingKey: Any one from: use a colorimeter to judge the end point; use a heat filter (water bath / glass of water) between lamp and tubes; carry out the experiment in a darkened room; repeat each test more times and calculate a mean (to improve reliability); test more values of the distance from the lamp (smaller intervals), especially near the turning point / extremes [1]

items.stem: Calcium ions are removed from the tissue fluid around a presynaptic knob. What is the effect?
items.answer: Acetylcholine is not released
items.markingKey: Ca²⁺ entry triggers exocytosis.

items.stem: Measurements on Mohammed, a healthy adult, gave: glomerular filtration rate 115 cm³ min⁻¹; urine production 1 cm³ min⁻¹; plasma glucose 5 mmol dm⁻³; urea concentration 0.25 g dm⁻³ in plasma and 16.8 g dm⁻³ in urine. Explain why the urea concentration in the urine is much higher than in the plasma.
items.answer: Most of the water in the filtrate is reabsorbed but most urea is not, so urea becomes concentrated.
items.markingKey: water reabsorbed [1]; urea retained [1] [2]

items.stem: Grace says: "F1 hybrid seeds can be saved and replanted to give the same high yield." Explain whether Grace is correct.
items.answer: The F2 generation shows segregation of alleles and loses the uniformity and hybrid vigour, so new F1 seed must be bought each year.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: The F2 generation shows segregation of alleles and loses the uniformity and hybrid vigour, so new F1 seed must be bought each year. [2]

items.stem: Lucas studies a strain of E. coli in which a mutation in the operator means the repressor cannot bind to it. Predict and explain the effect on the production of β-galactosidase.
items.answer: Β-galactosidase is made all the time, with or without lactose.
items.markingKey: prediction [1]; explanation in terms of repressor / operator / RNA polymerase [2] [3]

items.stem: Lucas isolated mitochondria from pigeon flight muscle and suspended them in a buffered solution containing pyruvate, ADP, Pi and oxygen. Over 20 minutes, 8 μmol of pyruvate were completely oxidised. (a) Calculate how many μmol of reduced NAD were formed. (b) Predict and explain the effect of removing oxygen from the suspension. (c) Name the location within the mitochondrion where the link reaction and Krebs cycle take place.
items.answer: (a) 32 μmol (b) CO₂ release would stop: no final electron acceptor, so reduced NAD/FAD are not oxidised; no NAD/FAD for the link reaction and Krebs cycle. (c) The matrix.
items.markingKey: (a) per pyruvate: 1 (link) + 3 (Krebs) = 4 [1]; 8 × 4 = 32 μmol [1] [2] (b) CO₂ release falls/stops [1]; no NAD regenerated [1]; dehydrogenation stops [1] [3] (c) The matrix [1]

items.stem: Grace amplified a DNA sample from a crime scene in Muscat. The reaction started with 1 copies of the target sequence and ran for 25 cycles, each lasting 2.5 minutes. (a) Calculate the number of copies of the target sequence after all cycles, assuming 100% efficiency. (b) Explain why the sample was amplified before DNA profiling. (c) Calculate how many cycles would be needed to obtain at least one million copies from one molecule.
items.answer: (a) 3.36 × 10⁷ (b) Only a tiny amount of DNA was present; PCR makes enough copies for analysis by electrophoresis. (c) 20 cycles
items.markingKey: (a) 1 × 2^25 [1] = 3.36 × 10⁷ [1] [2] (b) Only a tiny amount of DNA was present [1]; PCR makes enough copies for analysis by electrophoresis [1] [2] (c) 2^19 = 524 288; 2^20 = 1 048 576 [1]; 20 cycles [1] [2]

items.stem: Freya caught 60 field mice in a garden in Cape Town, marked each with a dot of non-toxic paint and released them. Two days later 60 were caught, of which 30 were marked. (a) Estimate the population size using the Lincoln index. (b) Explain why the marks must not make the animals more visible to predators.
items.answer: (a) 120 (b) Marked animals would be eaten more, so fewer marked recaptured, overestimating the population.
items.markingKey: (a) N = (n₁ × n₂) ÷ m₂ [1] = (60 × 60) ÷ 30 = 120 [1] [2] (b) fewer recaptured [1]; overestimate [1] [2]

items.stem: Researchers in Mumbai measured the action spectrum of a red alga from deep water. Unlike a typical land plant, its rate of photosynthesis was high at 560 nm, a wavelength that chlorophyll a absorbs poorly. (a) Suggest an explanation for the high rate of photosynthesis at this wavelength. (b) Explain why this is an advantage for the organism in its habitat.
items.answer: (a) The organism has accessory pigments (e.g. phycoerythrin / fucoxanthin) that absorb light at about 560 nm and pass the energy to chlorophyll a in the reaction centre. (b) Red and blue light are absorbed by water (or by the canopy), so the light reaching it is mainly green/blue-green; pigments that absorb these wavelengths allow photosynthesis.
items.markingKey: (a) accessory pigment [1]; absorbs this wavelength [1]; energy passed to reaction centre [1] [3] (b) light quality in habitat [1]; can use available wavelengths [1] [2]

items.stem: Tomás floated 10 mm sections cut from wheat coleoptiles in solutions of different auxin (IAA) concentrations for 24 hours in the dark, then measured their final lengths. Results table. IAA concentration / mg dm⁻³: 0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10. Mean increase in length / mm, trial 1: 0.9, 1, 2.1, 5.3, 5.3, 2.2; trial 2: 0.9, 1.5, 2.1, 5.1, 5.3, 2.2; trial 3: 0.9, 1, 2.1, 5.3, 4.9, 2.1. (a) Explain the results. (b) Suggest one way to improve this investigation.
items.answer: (a) Auxin stimulates proton pumping into the cell walls; the low pH activates expansins that loosen cellulose cross-links, so cells take up water and elongate; at very high concentrations auxin inhibits growth. (b) Use more sections per concentration.
items.markingKey: (a) proton pumping / acid growth [1]; expansins loosen walls [1]; inhibition at high concentration [1] [3] (b) Any one from: use more sections per concentration; measure with a ruler under a magnifying lens or use image analysis; remove the tips so the coleoptile does not produce its own auxin; repeat each test more times and calculate a mean (to improve reliability); test more values of the IAA concentration (smaller intervals), especially near the turning point / extremes [1]

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "continuous variation"?
options: Variation in which a characteristic falls into distinct categories with no intermediates, such as ABO blood group, usually controlled by one or a few genes.
A measure of the spread of data about the mean; about 68% of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean in a normal distribution.
One of several genes, each with a small additive effect, that together control a continuously variable characteristic.
Variation in which a characteristic has a range of values between two extremes, such as height, usually controlled by many genes and influenced by the environment.
items.answer: Variation in which a characteristic has a range of values between two extremes, such as height, usually controlled by many genes and influenced by the environment.
items.markingKey: Continuous variation: variation in which a characteristic has a range of values between two extremes, such as height, usually controlled by many genes and influenced by the environment.

items.stem: Why is gene therapy easier for recessive conditions than for dominant ones?
options: Recessive alleles are not expressed at all
Adding a functional dominant allele masks the faulty recessive one
items.answer: Adding a functional dominant allele masks the faulty recessive one
items.markingKey: A dominant faulty allele would still be expressed.

items.stem: DNP makes the inner mitochondrial membrane permeable to protons. What is the effect of DNP on respiring cells?
options: Oxygen uptake stops and ATP synthesis increases
Oxygen uptake continues but ATP synthesis falls and more heat is released
Both oxygen uptake and heat release fall
items.answer: Oxygen uptake continues but ATP synthesis falls and more heat is released
items.markingKey: DNP is an uncoupler.

items.stem: Hana drinks 1.5 dm³ of water. What happens next?
options: Less ADH is secreted and more dilute urine is produced
More ADH is secreted and less urine is produced
items.answer: Less ADH is secreted and more dilute urine is produced
items.markingKey: Blood water potential rises; ADH falls; fewer aquaporins.

items.stem: Explain how gibberellin brings about the mobilisation of starch in a germinating barley seed.
items.answer: Water uptake causes the embryo to release gibberellin; gibberellin diffuses to the aleurone layer; it causes breakdown of DELLA proteins so the transcription factor (PIF) can activate the amylase gene; amylase is secreted into the endosperm and hydrolyses starch to maltose, which is used by the embryo.
items.markingKey: GA from embryo [1]; aleurone [1]; DELLA broken down / gene transcribed [1]; amylase hydrolyses starch [1] [4]

items.stem: The classification of the honeybee is: Eukarya, ?, Arthropoda, Insecta, Hymenoptera, Apidae, Apis, mellifera. Which taxonomic rank is missing?
items.answer: Kingdom
items.markingKey: Order: domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species; missing rank = kingdom (Animalia).

items.stem: Explain why rubisco is often described as the most abundant protein on Earth.
items.answer: Rubisco is a slow enzyme (few reactions per second) and also reacts with oxygen, so leaves must contain very large amounts to fix enough CO₂.
items.markingKey: slow / low turnover [1]; large amounts needed [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain the effect on the lac operon if a mutation in the operator means the repressor cannot bind to it.
items.answer: Β-galactosidase is made all the time, with or without lactose.
items.markingKey: prediction [1]; explanation in terms of repressor / operator / RNA polymerase [2] [3]

items.stem: A population of 12 lizards was carried to a new island in Toronto's region by a storm. After 30 generations, the frequency of an allele for striped skin was 0.65, compared with 0.24 on the mainland. (a) Explain how the founder effect could account for this difference. (b) Explain how genetic drift could change the allele frequency further on the island.
items.answer: (a) The founders were a small, random sample of the mainland population, which by chance had a high frequency of the striped allele; the new population started with different allele frequencies and less genetic variation. (b) In a small population, random differences in which individuals reproduce change allele frequencies by chance from generation to generation; alleles may be lost or fixed.
items.markingKey: (a) small sample [1]; by chance not representative [1]; reduced variation [1] [3] (b) random / chance [1]; small population [1]; loss or fixation [1] [3]

items.stem: Amara amplified a DNA sample from a crime scene in Kuala Lumpur. The reaction started with 50 copies of the target sequence and ran for 15 cycles, each lasting 4 minutes. (a) Calculate the total time taken. (b) Suggest why the actual number of copies is lower than calculated. (c) Explain why the sample was amplified before DNA profiling. (d) Calculate how many cycles would be needed to obtain at least one million copies from one molecule.
items.answer: (a) 60 minutes (b) Primers or nucleotides are used up; Taq polymerase gradually loses activity; not every strand is copied each cycle (efficiency below 100%). (c) Only a tiny amount of DNA was present; PCR makes enough copies for analysis by electrophoresis. (d) 20 cycles
items.markingKey: (a) 15 × 4 = 60 min [1] (b) Primers or nucleotides are used up; Taq polymerase gradually loses activity; not every strand is copied each cycle (efficiency below 100%) [1] (c) Only a tiny amount of DNA was present [1]; PCR makes enough copies for analysis by electrophoresis [1] [2] (d) 2^19 = 524 288; 2^20 = 1 048 576 [1]; 20 cycles [1] [2]

items.stem: In 30 minutes, germinating wheat grains took in 3.2 cm³ of oxygen and gave out 2.73 cm³ of carbon dioxide. (a) Calculate the respiratory quotient and suggest which respiratory substrate is being used. (b) Calculate the rate of oxygen uptake per hour.
items.answer: (a) RQ = 0.85; a mixture of carbohydrate and lipid, as the RQ is close to the value for this substrate. (b) 6.4 cm³ h⁻¹
items.markingKey: (a) RQ = 2.73 ÷ 3.2 = 0.85 [1]; a mixture of carbohydrate and lipid [1]; reason linked to RQ value [1] [3] (b) 3.2 × 60 ÷ 30 = 6.4 [1]

items.stem: A clinician in Manila is investigating the effect of a drug (SGLT2 inhibitor) that blocks the sodium–glucose co-transporter in the PCT on kidney function. (a) Predict and explain the effect of the drug. (b) Describe the route taken by a molecule of urea from the blood in the glomerulus to the collecting duct.
items.answer: (a) Glucose would not be reabsorbed so it would appear in the urine; this lowers blood glucose in people with type 2 diabetes; more water would also be lost (osmotic effect). (b) Through pores in the capillary endothelium, the basement membrane and between podocytes into the Bowman's capsule; along the PCT, loop of Henle and DCT into the collecting duct.
items.markingKey: (a) glucose not reabsorbed [1]; glucose in urine [1]; lowers blood glucose / water loss [1] [3] (b) three filtration layers [1]; correct order of nephron regions [1] [2]

items.stem: In a myofibril studied by Elena, each myosin filament is 1.6 μm long and each actin filament extends 0.95 μm from the Z line. A relaxed sarcomere is 2.4 μm long; when contracted it is 2.1 μm long. (a) Calculate the total width of the I band (both halves) in the relaxed sarcomere. (b) Calculate the width of the H zone in the relaxed and contracted sarcomere.
items.answer: (a) 0.8 μm (b) relaxed 0.5 μm; contracted 0.2 μm
items.markingKey: (a) I band = sarcomere − A band = 2.4 − 1.6 [1] = 0.8 μm [1] [2] (b) H = sarcomere − 2 × actin length [1]; 0.5 and 0.2 μm [1] [2]

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "codominance"?
options: The location of a gene on the X chromosome, so that its inheritance pattern differs between males and females.
The existence of more than two alleles of a gene in a population, as in the ABO blood group gene.
A cross between an organism with a dominant phenotype and a homozygous recessive organism, used to find whether it is homozygous or heterozygous.
A situation in which both alleles in a heterozygote are fully expressed in the phenotype.
items.answer: A situation in which both alleles in a heterozygote are fully expressed in the phenotype.
items.markingKey: Codominance: a situation in which both alleles in a heterozygote are fully expressed in the phenotype.

items.stem: In the name Panthera leo, what does Panthera represent?
items.answer: The genus
items.markingKey: Binomial: Genus species.

items.stem: A plant in a dark room is lit by a single bulb. The distance from the lamp is reduced to a quarter. State and explain how the light intensity at the plant changes.
items.answer: The light intensity at the plant becomes 16 times bigger.
items.markingKey: Using light intensity ∝ 1/d²: light intensity at the plant ∝ distance from the lamp^−2.00; factor = 0.250^−2.00 = 16.0. 1 mark relationship, 1 mark conclusion.

items.stem: Grace drinks 1 dm³ of water. What happens next?
options: Less ADH is secreted and more dilute urine is produced
More ADH is secreted and less urine is produced
items.answer: Less ADH is secreted and more dilute urine is produced
items.markingKey: Blood water potential rises; ADH falls; fewer aquaporins.

items.stem: Omar says: "Methylene blue turns colourless because it is broken down by respiration." Explain whether Omar is correct.
items.answer: Methylene blue is reduced (accepts hydrogen from dehydrogenation reactions) and can be reoxidised to blue by shaking with air.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Methylene blue is reduced (accepts hydrogen from dehydrogenation reactions) and can be reoxidised to blue by shaking with air. [2]

items.stem: Felix floated 10 mm sections cut from wheat coleoptiles in solutions of different auxin (IAA) concentrations for 24 hours in the dark, then measured their final lengths. Results table. IAA concentration / mg dm⁻³: 0, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100. Mean increase in length / mm, trial 1: 0.9, 2, 4.9, 4.9, 2, 1; trial 2: 0.8, 1.9, 4.9, 4.9, 2, 0.9; trial 3: 0.9, 2.1, 4.9, 4.8, 2, 0.9. State two variables that should be kept constant in this investigation.
items.answer: Temperature; initial length of sections.
items.markingKey: Any two from: temperature; initial length of sections; age of coleoptiles; volume of solution; darkness (light breaks down auxin); sucrose concentration in solution [2]

items.stem: Mohammed says: "Two organisms that can mate must belong to the same species." Explain whether Mohammed is correct.
items.answer: They must produce fertile offspring; horses and donkeys mate but mules are infertile.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: They must produce fertile offspring; horses and donkeys mate but mules are infertile. [2]

items.stem: EcoRI recognises the sequence GAATTC and cuts it G^AATTC. The following single strand (5′→3′) of a linear double-stranded DNA molecule is to be cut: TTTGCTTCAGAATTCTCTGAAATTAGTACCCCTGAATTCTCGTAC. (a) State how many EcoRI sites are present and the lengths (in bases) of the fragments produced. (b) Explain why the recognition site is described as palindromic.
items.answer: (a) 2 sites; fragments of 10, 24, 11 bases (b) The sequence on one strand read 5′→3′ (GAATTC) is the same as the complementary strand read 5′→3′.
items.markingKey: (a) sites located [1]; fragment lengths 10, 24, 11 [1] [2] (b) The sequence on one strand read 5′→3′ (GAATTC) is the same as the complementary strand read 5′→3′ [1]

items.stem: A student in Muscat draws diagrams of meiosis in a cell with 2n = 6, in which one homologous pair carries alleles A and a, and another carries B and b. (a) Explain why gametes produced by meiosis are genetically different from each other while cells produced by mitosis are identical. (b) State the number of chromosomes in each cell at the end of meiosis II. (c) Suggest why errors in meiosis such as non-disjunction can lead to conditions such as Down syndrome.
items.answer: (a) Mitosis: no pairing, no crossing over, chromatids separate so daughter cells receive identical copies; meiosis: crossing over and independent assortment of homologues, plus halving of chromosome number. (b) 3 (c) If homologues or chromatids fail to separate, a gamete may have an extra chromosome; fertilisation gives a zygote with three copies (trisomy 21).
items.markingKey: (a) mitosis identical copies [1]; crossing over [1]; independent assortment [1] [3] (b) 3 [1] (c) non-disjunction [1]; extra chromosome / trisomy [1] [2]

items.stem: Freya sampled a school field in Lima using ten randomly placed 0.5 m × 0.5 m quadrats. Total numbers of each plant species: ryegrass 34, yarrow 40, moss 31, clover 2. (a) Calculate Simpson's index of diversity, D = 1 − Σ(n/N)². (b) State what the value of D indicates about the biodiversity of the area. (c) Calculate the mean density of the most common species per m², given that ten quadrats were used.
items.answer: (a) 0.675 (b) Relatively low biodiversity: D is well below 1, so one or two species dominate. (c) 16 per m²

items.stem: Yusuf separated the pigments in a leaf extract by thin-layer chromatography. The solvent front moved 11.5 cm. Three spots were seen: spot A (orange-yellow) 10.7 cm, spot B (yellow) 8.2 cm, spot C (yellow-green) 5.2 cm from the origin. Published Rf values for this solvent are: carotene: 0.95; phaeophytin: 0.81; xanthophyll: 0.71; chlorophyll a: 0.65; chlorophyll b: 0.45. (a) Calculate the Rf value of each spot. (b) Explain why the origin line is drawn in pencil and kept above the level of the solvent.
items.answer: (a) A 0.93; B 0.71; C 0.45 (b) Pencil (graphite) does not dissolve and run in the solvent; if the origin were below the solvent the pigments would dissolve into the solvent in the beaker.
items.markingKey: (a) distance ÷ solvent front [1]; all three correct [1] [2] (b) pencil insoluble [1]; pigments would dissolve into solvent [1] [2]

items.stem: A clinician in Cairo is investigating the effect of a drug that narrows the afferent arteriole on kidney function. (a) Predict and explain the effect of the drug. (b) Explain why the PCT cells contain many mitochondria.
items.answer: (a) Glomerular blood pressure would fall, so the rate of ultrafiltration (GFR) would decrease and less urine would be produced; urea would build up in the blood. (b) They provide ATP for active transport of Na⁺ out of the cells by the Na⁺/K⁺ pumps, which drives co-transport of glucose and amino acids.
items.markingKey: (a) lower hydrostatic pressure [1]; lower GFR [1]; consequence [1] [3] (b) ATP for active transport [1]; Na⁺ gradient for co-transport [1] [2]

items.stem: Elena reads that the complete oxidation of one mole of sucrose releases 5640 kJ of energy and yields about 68 mol of ATP. Hydrolysis of ATP releases 30.5 kJ mol⁻¹. (a) Calculate the percentage efficiency with which energy from the substrate is transferred to ATP. (b) Suggest why the actual yield of ATP per mole of substrate in a cell is often lower than the theoretical value.
items.answer: (a) 36.8% (b) Some protons leak back across the inner membrane without passing through ATP synthase; energy is used to transport ADP/Pi and pyruvate into the mitochondrion; some reduced NAD from glycolysis enters via a shuttle giving less ATP.
items.markingKey: (a) energy in ATP = 68 × 30.5 = 2074 kJ [1]; ÷ 5640 × 100 = 36.8% [1] [2] (b) proton leakage [1]; energy used for transport into mitochondrion / shuttle [1] [2]

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "the time after an action potential during which another action potential cannot be generated (or needs a larger stimulus)"?
items.answer: Refractory period
items.markingKey: Refractory period: the time after an action potential during which another action potential cannot be generated (or needs a larger stimulus).

items.stem: Why must a promoter be added with a gene inserted into a plasmid?
options: So that RNA polymerase can bind and transcribe the gene
items.answer: So that RNA polymerase can bind and transcribe the gene
items.markingKey: Without a promoter the gene is not expressed.

items.stem: A drug inhibits the enzyme that converts citrate to the 5C compound. Which substance will accumulate first?
items.answer: Citrate
items.markingKey: Substrate of the blocked step accumulates.

items.stem: The mean annual milk yield of dairy cows in a country rose from 4240 kg in 1970 to 8850 kg in 2020. What was the percentage increase?
Cholera toxin keeps G proteins permanently active. What would happen in a liver cell with active G proteins?
options: cAMP concentration would remain high and glycogen would be continually broken down
Glucagon could no longer bind to the cell
items.answer: cAMP concentration would remain high and glycogen would be continually broken down
items.markingKey: Adenylyl cyclase stays active.

items.stem: Freya placed a piece of Elodea in 0.5% sodium hydrogencarbonate solution at 25 °C and counted the bubbles released per minute with a lamp at different distances. Results table. Distance from the lamp / cm: 8, 12, 16, 20, 30, 40. Number of bubbles per minute, trial 1: 55, 49, 36, 27, 14, 9; trial 2: 55, 47, 35, 27, 14, 9; trial 3: 57, 46, 37, 28, 14, 9. State two variables that should be kept constant in this investigation.
items.answer: Temperature (use a water bath / heat filter); concentration of sodium hydrogencarbonate.
items.markingKey: Any two from: temperature (use a water bath / heat filter); concentration of sodium hydrogencarbonate; the same piece of pondweed; time allowed to adjust to each light intensity; background light (dark room) [3]

items.stem: Nadia says: "Crossing over happens between sister chromatids." Explain whether Nadia is correct.
items.answer: Crossing over happens between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes; sister chromatids are identical so exchange would not produce new combinations.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Crossing over happens between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes; sister chromatids are identical so exchange would not produce new combinations. [2]

items.stem: Sipho sampled a grazed pasture in Kathmandu using ten randomly placed 0.5 m × 0.5 m quadrats. Total numbers of each plant species: dandelion 13, ryegrass 30, daisy 28, buttercup 34, clover 22, plantain 14. (a) State what the value of D indicates about the biodiversity of the area. (b) Calculate the mean density of the most common species per m², given that ten quadrats were used.
items.answer: (a) Fairly high biodiversity: D is close to 1, so species richness and evenness are high. (b) 13.6 per m²
items.markingKey: (a) correct interpretation linked to value [1] (b) area sampled = 10 × 0.25 = 2.5 m² [1]; 34 ÷ 2.5 = 13.6 per m² [1] [2]

items.stem: A health clinic in Istanbul is explaining how a progesterone-only pill works to a group of students. (a) Explain why the pill must be taken at about the same time each day. (b) Suggest one social or ethical issue linked to the use of oral contraceptives. (c) Describe the role of the hypothalamus in the menstrual cycle.
items.answer: (a) Synthetic hormones are broken down; regular doses keep their concentrations high enough to suppress FSH and LH. (b) Allows control of family size / women's careers; side effects and health risks (e.g. thrombosis); religious objections; no protection against STIs. (c) It secretes GnRH, which stimulates the anterior pituitary to release FSH and LH; it responds to oestrogen and progesterone feedback.
items.markingKey: (a) Synthetic hormones are broken down [1]; regular doses keep their concentrations high enough to suppress FSH and LH [1] [2] (b) any 2 from: Allows control of family size / women's careers; side effects and health risks (e.g. thrombosis); religious objections; no protection against STIs (1 mark each) [2] (c) It secretes GnRH, which stimulates the anterior pituitary to release FSH and LH [1]; it responds to oestrogen and progesterone feedback [1] [2]

items.stem: cDNA from cancer cells was labelled with a red fluorescent dye and cDNA from normal cells of the same tissue with a green dye. Both were mixed and applied to a microarray. The spots for four genes were: gene U green, gene S green, gene P black, gene R yellow. (a) State what each colour shows about the expression of each gene. (b) Explain why cDNA was made from mRNA rather than using genomic DNA. (c) Explain how the cDNA binds to particular spots on the microarray.
items.answer: (a) gene U: expressed only (or much more) in the normal cells; gene S: expressed only (or much more) in the normal cells; gene P: not expressed in either; gene R: expressed equally in both (b) mRNA is present only for genes being expressed (transcribed); genomic DNA contains all genes whether expressed or not. (c) Each spot contains many copies of a single-stranded probe; cDNA hybridises by complementary base pairing to its matching probe.
items.markingKey: (a) two correct [1]; all correct [1] [2] (b) mRNA shows expression [1]; DNA has all genes [1] [2] (c) Each spot contains many copies of a single-stranded probe [1]; cDNA hybridises by complementary base pairing to its matching probe [1] [2]

items.stem: Grace placed 10 g of woodlice in a respirometer containing soda lime at 25 °C. The coloured fluid in the capillary tube (internal diameter 0.8 mm) moved 24 mm in 5 minutes. (a) Calculate the volume of oxygen taken up, in mm³. (b) Explain why the fluid moved towards the organisms.
items.answer: (a) 12.1 mm³ (b) Oxygen was taken up and the CO₂ released was absorbed by the soda lime, so the volume (pressure) of gas in the tube fell.
items.markingKey: (a) radius = 0.4 mm [1]; π × 0.4² × 24 = 12.1 mm³ [1] [2] (b) O₂ used [1]; CO₂ absorbed so volume falls [1] [2]

items.stem: Omar measured the height or mass of individuals in a population of maize plants in Manila and found that the data formed a normal distribution. (a) Explain why the data form a normal distribution. (b) Explain the difference between variation caused by genes and variation caused by the environment in terms of whether it can be inherited.
items.answer: (a) The characteristic shows continuous variation: it is controlled by many genes (polygenes) with additive effects, plus environmental effects; most individuals are near the mean with few at the extremes. (b) Genetic variation is passed to offspring in gametes; environmental variation is not inherited (it changes the phenotype, not the alleles).
items.markingKey: (a) polygenic [1]; additive / environment [1]; most near mean [1] [3] (b) Genetic variation is passed to offspring in gametes [1]; environmental variation is not inherited (it changes the phenotype, not the alleles) [1] [2]

items.stem: Zara floated epidermal strips from a broad bean leaf on solutions of different ABA concentrations in bright light for 1 hour, then measured the stomatal aperture of 10 stomata using an eyepiece graticule. Results table. ABA concentration / μmol dm⁻³: 0, 0.5, 2, 8, 32. Mean stomatal aperture / μm, trial 1: 12.6, 9.9, 7.8, 5.3, 3.5; trial 2: 17.9, 10.5, 8.3, 5, 3.3; trial 3: 12.3, 10.6, 7.6, 5.5, 3.4. (a) Identify the anomalous result in the table and state what should be done with it. (b) State the type of graph you would draw to display these results and what you would plot on each axis.
items.answer: (a) Trial 2 at 0 μmol dm⁻³ (17.9 μm); it should be ignored when calculating the mean (or repeated). (b) A line graph: ABA concentration on the x-axis and mean mean stomatal aperture on the y-axis.
items.markingKey: (a) trial 2 at 0 μmol dm⁻³ identified [1]; ignore / repeat it [1] [2] (b) line graph (continuous independent variable) [1]; ABA concentration on x-axis and mean stomatal aperture on y-axis [1] [2]

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "PCR"?
options: A technique that separates DNA fragments by size by moving them through an agarose gel in an electric field.
The polymerase chain reaction: a method of making many copies of a specific DNA sequence by cycles of denaturation, annealing and extension.
A heat-stable DNA polymerase from the bacterium Thermus aquaticus, used in PCR because it is not denatured at 95 °C.
A short single-stranded DNA sequence complementary to the end of the target sequence, which allows DNA polymerase to start copying.
items.answer: The polymerase chain reaction: a method of making many copies of a specific DNA sequence by cycles of denaturation, annealing and extension.
items.markingKey: PCR: the polymerase chain reaction: a method of making many copies of a specific DNA sequence by cycles of denaturation, annealing and extension.

items.stem: What is the main purpose of converting pyruvate to lactate in mammalian muscle during anaerobic respiration?
options: To regenerate NAD so glycolysis can continue
To store energy as lactate for growth
items.answer: To regenerate NAD so glycolysis can continue
items.markingKey: Reduced NAD is reoxidised.

items.stem: Explain why a cross between two individuals with sickle cell trait gives a 1 : 2 : 1 ratio of phenotypes.
items.answer: Alleles Hbᴬ and Hbˢ are codominant, so heterozygotes have a distinct phenotype (sickle cell trait); HbᴬHbˢ × HbᴬHbˢ gives 1 HbᴬHbᴬ : 2 HbᴬHbˢ : 1 HbˢHbˢ, each a different phenotype.
items.markingKey: codominance [1]; genotype ratio = phenotype ratio [1] [2]

items.stem: In a myofibril studied by Ethan, each myosin filament is 1.6 μm long and each actin filament extends 0.95 μm from the Z line. A relaxed sarcomere is 2.6 μm long; when contracted it is 2 μm long. What is the width of the A band in the contracted sarcomere?
items.answer: 1.6 μm
items.markingKey: A band = length of myosin = 1.6 μm in any state.

items.stem: Which threat to biodiversity does CITES aim to reduce?
items.answer: Overexploitation through international trade
items.markingKey: Trade in endangered species.

items.stem: Jonas supplies a culture of cyanobacteria with radioactive ¹⁴CO₂ and measures the radioactivity in GP and RuBP. Then the light intensity is increased (CO₂ still high). Predict and explain the changes in GP and RuBP.
items.answer: GP falls slightly and RuBP rises: more ATP and reduced NADP so GP is reduced faster and RuBP regenerated faster.
items.markingKey: prediction: GP falls slightly and RuBP rises [1]; explanation: more ATP and reduced NADP so GP is reduced faster and RuBP regenerated faster [2] [3]

items.stem: Freya says: "F1 hybrid seeds can be saved and replanted to give the same high yield." Explain whether Freya is correct.
items.answer: The F2 generation shows segregation of alleles and loses the uniformity and hybrid vigour, so new F1 seed must be bought each year.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: The F2 generation shows segregation of alleles and loses the uniformity and hybrid vigour, so new F1 seed must be bought each year. [5]

items.stem: Measurements on Felix, a healthy adult, gave: glomerular filtration rate 110 cm³ min⁻¹; urine production 1.2 cm³ min⁻¹; plasma glucose 4.5 mmol dm⁻³; urea concentration 0.35 g dm⁻³ in plasma and 17.7 g dm⁻³ in urine. (a) Calculate how many times more concentrated urea is in the urine than in the plasma. (b) Explain why the urea concentration in the urine is much higher than in the plasma.
items.answer: (a) 51 times (b) Most of the water in the filtrate is reabsorbed but most urea is not, so urea becomes concentrated.
items.markingKey: (a) 17.7 ÷ 0.35 = 51 [1] (b) water reabsorbed [1]; urea retained [1] [2]

items.stem: A company in Santiago produces human growth hormone for treating growth hormone deficiency using genetically modified bacteria. (a) Explain why mRNA is extracted from cells of the anterior pituitary rather than using the gene from chromosomal DNA. (b) Explain the advantages of producing human growth hormone using genetically modified bacteria.
items.answer: (a) These cells make the protein so contain many copies of its mRNA; mRNA has no introns, so the cDNA made from it can be expressed by bacteria. (b) Identical to human protein so fewer immune reactions; large quantities quickly and cheaply in fermenters; no risk of infection from animal/human sources; no ethical issues of using animals.
items.markingKey: (a) abundant mRNA in these cells [1]; no introns [1]; bacteria cannot splice [1] [3] (b) any 3 from: Identical to human protein so fewer immune reactions; large quantities quickly and cheaply in fermenters; no risk of infection from animal/human sources; no ethical issues of using animals (1 mark each) [3]

items.stem: Calculate how many molecules of reduced NAD are produced in glycolysis from 2 molecules of glucose. Show your working, treating each stage separately.
items.markingKey: glycolysis: 2 per glucose; × 2 = 4. Per-stage values [1]; correct total [1] [2]

items.stem: Zara is studying meiosis in a pea plant, which has a diploid number of 14. (a) Calculate the number of possible chromosome combinations in a zygote formed by random fertilisation of two such gametes. (b) Explain why the actual number of genetically different gametes is much greater than this.
items.answer: (a) 16,384 (1.64 × 10⁴) (b) Crossing over during prophase I produces new combinations of alleles within chromosomes.
items.markingKey: (a) (2ⁿ)² = 128² [1] = 1.64 × 10⁴ [1] [2] (b) crossing over [1]; new combinations of alleles on chromatids [1] [2]

items.stem: In multiple sclerosis, the myelin sheath of neurones in the CNS is damaged by the immune system. (a) Explain the effect on the transmission of nerve impulses. (b) Explain how the resting potential is restored after an action potential.
items.answer: (a) Saltatory conduction is lost in damaged regions; impulses travel more slowly or are blocked because local circuits cannot reach the next node. (b) K⁺ diffuse out through K⁺ channels (repolarisation); Na⁺/K⁺ pump uses ATP to move 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in to restore the ion concentrations.
items.markingKey: (a) Saltatory conduction is lost in damaged regions; impulses travel more slowly or are blocked because local circuits cannot reach the next node. [3] (b) K⁺ out [1]; pump restores gradients [1] [2]

items.stem: Felix separated the pigments in a leaf extract by thin-layer chromatography. The solvent front moved 7.1 cm. Three spots were seen: spot A (yellow) 5 cm, spot B (blue-green) 4.5 cm, spot C (yellow-green) 3.4 cm from the origin. Published Rf values for this solvent are: carotene: 0.95; phaeophytin: 0.81; xanthophyll: 0.71; chlorophyll a: 0.65; chlorophyll b: 0.45. (a) Calculate the Rf value of each spot. (b) Use the Rf values to identify the pigments.
items.answer: (a) A 0.7; B 0.63; C 0.48 (b) A = xanthophyll; B = chlorophyll a; C = chlorophyll b
items.markingKey: (a) distance ÷ solvent front [1]; all three correct [1] [2] (b) two correct [1]; all three [1] [2]
